Improve telemetry (clarity and design)

[PostHog's strategy](https://posthog.com/handbook/strategy) is to focus everything we have for at least the next 6-12 months (and likely, beyond that), on making the Community Edition awesome and very popular.

PostHog currently uses PostHog to track itself where users haven't opted themselves out.

We believe tracking Daily Active Users is the most meaningful top metric to check if we are achieving our strategy. That's because it's the combination of (i) new users signing up and (ii) existing users sticking around.

We currently have basic telemetry in the product for **non-opted out** users (anyone can opt out at any time). We use PostHog to track the following:

* new PostHog user signed up - name, email and company name entered
  * = used to produce unique sign ups
* pageviews for PostHog users when they come back to the product
  * = used to produce DAUs

The challenge

There is no fine grained control for users over this telemetry:

* You can opt out of nothing or everything, and the opt out is on the /settings page where most users go to set up the product
* If a single user opts out, they opt out of (i) aggregated data (ii) identifiable data (ii) their entire team

This means almost every engaged user that we know of anecdotally has (understandably) opted out of our tracking.

We also are not clear over exactly how our telemetry works (we have just moved docs and need to add a new section for this - legacy [explanation](https://docs.posthog.com/#/product-direction)), and should clarify things. For example, if it is left on, we do not collect users' user data, which is probably important for people to know :)

Proposal

I would like us to (i) make it easier to remove personally identifiable information from our tracking but (ii) make it more likely people leave anonymized "counter" style tracking to let us assess page views properly.

There are several conditions that we would need to meet for this to be responsible:

* If a user is opted out, that user shall forever remain opted out of everything
* We should explain clearly in our new docs what the telemetry does
* We should raise this in the community first to give people a chance to talk about it

To solve this, I'd suggest:

1. we create a page somewhere that is specific to our telemetry in the app, as the regular settings page is becoming complex Ie setup>advanced.

* That page makes clear exactly what is tracked and what isn't.
* This page lets you opt out of the data categories we track in a more fine-grained way:
  * Team level (ideally this would only come from an admin role)
  * User and field level

2. We track anonymized aggregated usage information by default, but provide a code level change to manage this, that we would explain how to do in the docs. Just the minimum info would be collected to work out anonyized DAUs. I'd see that as the only cost of the free software, which helps us keep raising money and building cool stuff.

Why I think this is the right direction

If PostHog can track DAUs, we're much better able to explain the software's popularity to investors. There is significant social good in this - it lets us build a powerful, stable and well supported product and community.

However, our mini group of employees are not the only people in the community and I want to get feedback from anyone reading this before implementing it. Do you agree? Else, could you suggest a different approach to the challenge above?

Slack agent: thread follow-ups fail with "GitHub user integration requires reauthorization"

For PostHog users who have **not** connected a personal GitHub account to their PostHog user, the Slack agent answers the first message in a thread normally, then fails every follow-up in that thread with:

> **Task Failed** :x:
> GitHub user integration for this run requires reauthorization
> Reply in this thread with `retry` to try again from the latest checkpoint, or add instructions to change the approach.

Replying `retry` fails the same way within seconds. Users with a personal GitHub account connected are unaffected, so to the affected user this reads as a random product fault: the first turn always works, the project's GitHub integration is healthy, and the thread often needs no repository at all.

1. Connect the project's GitHub integration, so the team has a working GitHub App installation.
2. Use a PostHog user that has **no** personal GitHub account linked under their own user settings.
3. As that user, mention the PostHog app in a Slack channel and ask any question. The first turn answers normally.
4. Post a follow-up in the same thread. It fails with the error above, and `retry` fails identically.

Root cause: a task created by someone with no usable personal GitHub is frozen as bot-authored in the initial run's state ([`models.py:893-899`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/e3540bb9fa12b49508a12dc5ddcb6f7edf892f65/products/tasks/backend/models.py#L893-L899)), which is why the first turn works on the team installation token. A Slack follow-up creates a new run and rebuilds its state without carrying `pr_authorship_mode` ([`task_creation.py:1294-1343`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/e3540bb9fa12b49508a12dc5ddcb6f7edf892f65/posthog/temporal/ai/slack_app/activities/task_creation.py#L1294-L1343)), so the mode re-derives to `USER`, credential resolution finds no personal integration, and the Slack-only branch raises instead of falling back to the team token ([`utils.py:1177-1182`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/e3540bb9fa12b49508a12dc5ddcb6f7edf892f65/products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/utils.py#L1177-L1182)). The cloud resume path re-resolves the mode and does not have this problem ([`api.py:4744-4760`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/e3540bb9fa12b49508a12dc5ddcb6f7edf892f65/products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py#L4744-L4760)), so carrying or re-resolving `pr_authorship_mode` on the Slack resume looks like the fix.

Telemetry matches: first turns never fail with this error, follow-ups from users without a personal GitHub always do, and follow-ups from a different Slack user than the thread starter are not the trigger. Reproduced internally on 2026-08-24.

Worth fixing alongside: the error copy points at the wrong remedy (there is no integration to reauthorize, and `retry` rebuilds the same state), and the captured exception carries no team or user identity, which makes the failure hard to attribute.

No open PR, merged fix, or existing issue covers this.

Enriched flag analytics: $feature_interaction alone never unlocks the Usage tab charts

Docs (`posthog.com/docs/libraries/js/usage#enriched-flag-analytics`) present `$feature_view` and `$feature_interaction` as one feature: send either or both to get two extra charts on a flag's Usage tab ("Feature viewed total volume" and "Feature interaction total volume").

In practice, only `$feature_view` unlocks them. `find_flags_with_enriched_analytics` in `products/feature_flags/backend/flag_analytics.py` queries:

```python
WHERE timestamp between %(begin)s AND %(end)s AND event = '$feature_view'
```

An app that sends `$feature_interaction` but never `$feature_view` never flips `has_enriched_analytics`, so it never sees either chart — even though it's sending exactly what the docs describe as half the feature.

Either:
- Have the query also match `$feature_interaction` (`event IN ('$feature_view', '$feature_interaction')`), so sending either event unlocks the charts, matching what the docs promise. Or
- If `$feature_view` is intentionally required as the trigger, say so explicitly in the docs instead of presenting the two events as interchangeable.

'Matching events' when using 'Element matches HTML selector' in Actions lies to users

The string you put in the `Element matches HTML selector` section of actions is just searched among the elements chain in ClickHouse. This makes sense! Parsing and selecting based on CSS at read time across all events in CH would be too slow.

The problem is that it lies to users, they see `Matching events` and get confused when their action doesn't fire (often they are expecting a Webhook send).

In the example above, the user entered `foo`, thinking it would hit elements with the `foo` class in their HTML. They see matches, are happy, and hit save. The problem is that a plain string CSS selector searches for *elements*, i.e. `<foo>`, to select a class they needed to put `.foo`. Nothing will actually match and the action won't fire.

Our CSS selector logic [is already implemented in TypeScript in the plugin-server](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/72b7077ecf497ef231c67a009776c40fd34d5f0d/plugin-server/src/worker/ingestion/action-matcher.ts#L470). What if we shared the code with the frontend and filtered out matching events on the front-end? It wouldn't be perfect, but it would avoid these common false positives.

Alternatively, or in addition to, we could have a very loud message/banner near `Matching events` when the CSS selector is non-empty.

Workaround Needed for Cookie Validation Issue During Django Upgrade

We've encountered an issue related to two-factor authentication cookie validation after a major Django version upgrade, as detailed in issue [#686](https://github.com/jazzband/django-two-factor-auth/issues/686). This issue arises due to the change in user password hashes when Django's hash iteration count is updated in a new version, leading to a mismatch in the two-factor authentication cookies' validation.

We can for now implement a workaround. This involves catching the `BadSignature` exception raised during the cookie validation process when there's a mismatch in the hashes. This situation occurs after upgrading Django, which causes the user's password hash to change, thereby invalidating the existing two-factor authentication cookies.

This issue is critical for us to upgrade our Django version without disrupting the user experience of people coming back and having a 2FA cookie.

bug(llma): Type mismatch error in traces query when filtering by `$ai_is_error`

The traces query API returns a ClickHouse type mismatch error when querying events with the `$ai_is_error` property:

```
There is no supertype for types String, UInt8 because some of them are String/FixedString/Enum and some of them are not: while executing 'FUNCTION equals(__table1.mat_$ai_is_error :: 7, 1_UInt8 :: 34)
```

This occurs because the materialized column `mat_$ai_is_error` is type `Nullable(String)` but the query compares it to boolean `true` (which ClickHouse converts to `UInt8`).

1. Run PostHog locally with ClickHouse
2. Send AI events with `$ai_is_error` property set to `true`
3. Query the traces API endpoint
4. Observe the type mismatch error

Root cause

File: `posthog/hogql_queries/ai/traces_query_runner.py:258`

The query uses:
```python
properties.$ai_is_error = true
```

But the materialized column (created in migration 0176) is `Nullable(String)` type, and the actual data is stored as the string `"true"` in JSON properties.

When HogQL resolves `properties.$ai_is_error`, it uses the materialized column, causing a String vs UInt8 type mismatch.

Fix

Change the comparison to use string literal:
```python
properties.$ai_is_error = 'true'
```

This aligns with:
- The materialized column type
- The actual data format (string "true")
- Other queries in the codebase that already use string comparison

Migration 0176 created the materialized column as:
```python
ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS `mat_$ai_is_error` Nullable(String)
```

Log-alert destinations cannot be edited (Save / per-kind toggle fail; alert API has no update)

There is no supported way to **edit** a log-alert notification destination after create. The UI still presents an editor, per-kind Active switches, and copy that says you can change headers / body / filters. Every write goes to the generic hog-functions API and is rejected:

> Alert notification destinations are managed through the alert API.

The alert destinations API that message points at only supports **create** and **delete of the whole HogFunction group**. It cannot update URL, headers, enabled flags, or which event kinds notify.

That is the product bug. Save / toggle failures are the UI hitting a write path that does not exist.

Example Cloud pages (EU, project `117388`, alert `workers`):

- Alert notifications: https://eu.posthog.com/project/117388/logs/alerts/01a04724-65dc-743b-ac2f-18bb68cfb5ab/notifications/01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403
- HogFunction editor (Save): https://eu.posthog.com/project/117388/functions/01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403?returnTo=%2Flogs%2Falerts%2F01a04724-65dc-743b-ac2f-18bb68cfb5ab%2Fnotifications%2F01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403

1. Logs → Alerts → open an alert that has a webhook destination → Notifications → open the destination.
2. Toggle **Active** on Firing (or Resolved / Auto-disabled / Errored).
3. Toast: `Failed to pause notification: Alert notification destinations are managed through the alert API.` Switch snaps back to Active.
4. Click **Open editor**. Page copy: *"These hog functions only run for this alert. Open one to edit the message body, headers, filters, or destination details…"*
5. Change Headers (e.g. add `Authorization`) or any other field → **Save**.
6. Trigger field shows the same validation error; Save does not persist. `PATCH /api/projects/:id/hog_functions/:id/` with `{ "enabled": false }` or `{ "inputs": … }` returns the same 400 (`field: filters`).
7. `POST /api/projects/:id/hog_functions/` with `type=internal_destination`, `template-webhook`, and `$logs_alert_firing` + `alert_id` is rejected the same way.
8. `POST /api/projects/:id/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/` accepts only `type` + Slack fields or `webhook_url`. No `headers`, `enabled`, or `event_kinds`. Always creates all four kinds. No destination `PATCH`. Delete is atomic for the whole group.

**Why this is one issue.** [#84149](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/84149) (closed) and [#84285](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/84285) fixed **reads** of managed destinations. The write guard was called deliberate. The leftover hole is: users still need to change a destination, and nothing can.

**What users cannot do today (all the same gap):**

| Need | Blocked by |
| --- | --- |
| Custom webhook headers (Bearer / HMAC) | Create hardcodes `WEBHOOK_HEADERS` (`Content-Type`, `X-PostHog-Webhook-Version: 1`) in `products/alerts/backend/destination_configs.py`. Hog-functions PATCH refused. |
| Firing-only (skip resolved / errored / auto-disabled) | `create_destination` always loops `EVENT_KINDS`. Cannot delete one kind. Cannot `enabled: false` one HogFunction. |
| Pause / resume one kind | LemonSwitch → `api.hogFunctions.update({ enabled })` → write guard. |
| Change URL / body / filters in place | No destination update. Terraform provider documents the same: delete + recreate, with a window of no notifications. |

**Where the UI lies**

- `LogsAlertNotificationDetailScene.tsx` — per-kind `logs-alert-destination-toggle-*` → `setHogFunctionEnabled` → `api.hogFunctions.update`.
- `logsAlertNotificationDetailSceneLogic.ts` — lists via `api.hogFunctions.list`; toggle/save never call the alert destinations API.
- HogFunction configuration Save → `submitConfiguration` → same hog-functions PATCH.
- Insight-alert destinations *can* be edited via hog-functions because `$insight_alert_firing` is carved out of `is_managed_alert_internal_event`. `$logs_alert_*` is not.

**Write guard** (`products/cdp/backend/api/hog_function.py`): any create/update whose filters include a managed `$…_alert_(firing\|resolved\|errored\|auto_disabled\|match)` event is refused unless `allow_managed_alert_destination` is set. Only the logs alert destinations **create** path sets that flag.

**Alert destinations API surface** (`products/logs/backend/presentation/views/alerts_api.py`):

- `POST …/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/` — create only (`LogsAlertCreateDestinationSerializer`: `type`, slack_*, `webhook_url`).
- `POST …/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/delete/` — atomic group delete.
- `GET …/destinations/` (if shipped) — read.
- No `PATCH` / update.

Related: [#84149](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/84149) (read exclusion, closed), [#84285](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/84285) (GET destinations), [terraform `posthog_logs_alert_destination`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PostHog/posthog/latest/docs/resources/logs_alert_destination) ("PostHog has no update endpoint for destinations"). [#45336](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/45336) is about having log alerts at all, not editing destinations.

**Suggested direction**

1. Add destination **update** on the alert API (the only writer the guard allows): at least `webhook_url`, custom headers, and which event kinds are enabled (or per-kind `enabled`). Keep create/delete atomic if the group invariant still matters.
2. Point the notifications UI (Save, Active switches, editor) at that API instead of `api.hogFunctions.update`.
3. Until then, hide or disable Save / Open editor / per-kind toggles and drop the "edit headers" copy so the UI matches the API.

A custom / non-managed HogFunction cannot subscribe to `$logs_alert_*` either: the CDP internal-event consumer only invokes a function whose filters include the exact event id plus `alert_id`, and creating that filter is what the write guard blocks.

team_metadata cache verification loses most scheduled runs to DEFAULT queue starvation

`verify_and_fix_team_metadata_cache_task` is scheduled hourly with `expires_seconds=60 * 60` and runs on the shared `DEFAULT` celery queue. When that queue's backlog exceeds an hour, the beat message expires before a worker picks it up, and the worker discards it on receipt instead of executing it.

Completions over the last 24h (2026-08-10):

| Task | Queue | Scheduled/day | prod-us | prod-eu |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verify_and_fix_team_metadata_cache_task` | `DEFAULT` | 24 | **2** | **12** |
| `verify_and_fix_flag_definitions_cache_task` | `FEATURE_FLAGS_LONG_RUNNING` | 24 | 15 | 23 |
| `verify_and_fix_flags_cache_task` | `FEATURE_FLAGS_LONG_RUNNING` | 48 | 31 | 40 |

flag_definitions is a controlled comparison: same hourly cadence, same 1h expiry, different queue only. A 14-day back-test on 2026-08-06 (run while validating alert windows for PostHog/charts#14042) showed the same shape: 2-8 completions/day for team_metadata in prod-us.

Numbers from `sum by (task_name) (increase(posthog_celery_task_success_total{task_name=~"posthog.tasks.hypercache_verification.verify_and_fix_.*"}[24h]))`. Some baseline loss on all three tasks is expected (deploys kill in-flight runs); the team_metadata gap is the queue.

Why nobody noticed

An expired task never executes, so nothing fires: no `posthog_celery_task_failure_total` increment, no exception capture, no log line from the task. The success counter just quietly fails to increment. Lock-contention skips return cleanly and count as successes, so they cannot explain the gap; these runs are genuinely discarded.

Impact

- The sweep is the self-heal backstop for stale or missing team-metadata cache entries. Designed repair latency is roughly an hour; actual prod-us latency is many hours (2 completions/day means gaps of 12h or more).
- The `FlagsCacheVerificationNotRunning` alert (PostHog/charts#14042) needs a 36h window on its team_metadata arm to avoid false-firing on this starvation, so a full stall of the task would take a day and a half to page. The alert spec says to tighten toward ~4h once this is fixed.
- team_metadata is just the task we measured. Everything else on the prod-us DEFAULT queue sees the same delays, and any other periodic task scheduled with an expiry is presumably also losing runs the same silent way.

1. Move `verify_and_fix_team_metadata_cache_task` to `CeleryQueue.FEATURE_FLAGS_LONG_RUNNING`, matching its two siblings ([one line](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/7ebf3a6be217744f628689439b05413a6cbdd946/posthog/tasks/hypercache_verification.py#L226)). Its 20-min soft limit fits that queue's profile, and the flags task already runs there at twice the cadence.
2. Once completions reach ~24/day in both regions, tighten the charts alert window from 36h toward ~4h.
3. Separately: audit prod-us DEFAULT queue capacity, and consider alerting on scheduled-vs-completed deltas for expiry-bearing periodic tasks so the next case of this is found by a monitor instead of by accident.

Refs: [schedule + expiry](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/7ebf3a6be217744f628689439b05413a6cbdd946/posthog/tasks/scheduled.py#L410-L416), [queue assignments](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/7ebf3a6be217744f628689439b05413a6cbdd946/posthog/tasks/hypercache_verification.py#L202-L250).

The LLM Analytics **trace view** renders the same generation multiple times and inflates the trace's token/cost totals, for traces whose `$ai_generation` events have no `$ai_span_id`.

**Observed** (PostHog Cloud US, project 222862):

- Trace `caption-chat-kh7ayjbhs3wdf7thdjh2f2avqn8a78za-1783636807880` shows **two** identical generation nodes in the tree (gpt-5-mini, 582→353 tokens, 3.9s each) and a header of `1164 → 706 (Σ 1870)` — exactly 2× the real single call.

experiment archive response echoes stale (pre-mutation) feature_flag state when disable_feature_flag=true

`POST /api/projects/:id/experiments/:id/archive/` with `disable_feature_flag: true` correctly disables and archives the linked feature flag in the database, but the **response body echoes the pre-mutation flag state**. The embedded `feature_flag` object comes back with `active: true` and `archived: false` even though the row is now disabled and archived.

This is a stale-serialization bug, not a data bug — the DB is correct. But an API client that trusts the response (rather than re-fetching the flag) is misled into thinking the flag is still live.

Repro

Archive an ended experiment whose flag is still active:

```
POST /api/projects/1/experiments/87/archive/
{ "disable_feature_flag": true }
```

Response (trimmed):

```yaml
archived: true          # correct
feature_flag:
  active: true          # WRONG — the row is actually inactive
  deleted: false        # WRONG — the row is actually archived
```

Re-fetching the flag (`GET .../feature_flags/?search=<key>&archived=true`) confirms it is really `ARCHIVED` / inactive. Only the archive response is stale.

Root cause

In `_archive_linked_feature_flag` the flag is mutated through a **separately fetched** `FeatureFlag` instance:

https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/experiments/backend/experiment_service.py#L1595-L1641

```python
feature_flag = (
    FeatureFlag.objects.select_for_update()
    .filter(pk=experiment.feature_flag_id, team_id=experiment.team_id)
    .first()
)
archive_flag(feature_flag, team=self.team, user=self.user, request=request, disable_if_active=disable_if_active)
```

`archive_flag` saves *that* instance. But the `experiment` object returned to the view still holds its own cached forward relation `experiment.feature_flag` — a different Python object, loaded before the mutation. The view then serializes the stale experiment:

https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/experiments/backend/presentation/views.py#L444-L450

```python
archived_experiment = service.archive_experiment(experiment, disable_feature_flag=..., ...)
return Response(ExperimentSerializer(archived_experiment, context=self.get_serializer_context()).data)
```

`ExperimentSerializer` reads `archived_experiment.feature_flag`, which is the cached pre-mutation instance, so the nested flag reflects the old state.

After the gated write, assign the refreshed instance back onto the experiment's cached relation so the serializer reads current state:

```python
archive_flag(feature_flag, team=self.team, user=self.user, request=request, disable_if_active=disable_if_active)
experiment.feature_flag = feature_flag  # keep the serialized relation in sync with the mutated row
```

(`experiment.refresh_from_db()` in the view would also work but is heavier and drops other in-memory state.)

Worth a look at the sibling paths that mutate the flag through a re-fetched instance and return the experiment — **unarchive** (`unarchive_experiment` / `_unarchive_linked_feature_flag`) has the same shape and likely the same staleness in reverse.

Test gap

The existing archive-with-disable test asserts the **DB row**, not the response body, so it passes despite the stale echo:

https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/experiments/backend/test/test_presentation_api.py#L5182-L5186

```python
self.assertEqual(archive_response.status_code, status.HTTP_200_OK)
feature_flag = FeatureFlag.objects.get(id=feature_flag_id)   # re-fetches from DB
self.assertFalse(feature_flag.active)
self.assertTrue(feature_flag.archived)
```

Add assertions on the response body itself:

```python
body_flag = archive_response.json()["feature_flag"]
self.assertFalse(body_flag["active"])
self.assertTrue(body_flag["archived"])
```

Found while exercising the full experiment lifecycle through the PostHog MCP (`experiment-archive` tool). The MCP tool description says the flag is "also disabled and archived," and it is — the response just doesn't reflect it.

fix(clickhouse): align inserted_at nullability on events_recent / distributed_events_recent with their storage table

The `Distributed` tables `events_recent` and `distributed_events_recent` declare `inserted_at` as `Nullable(DateTime64(6, 'UTC'))`, but their underlying storage table `sharded_events_recent` declares it **non-null** (`DateTime64(6, 'UTC') DEFAULT now64()`). A `Distributed` table is a metadata-only routing layer and its column types should mirror the storage table, so the `Nullable(...)` wrapper is schema drift: the proxy advertises a column as possibly-NULL that is in fact never NULL (storage is non-null with a `DEFAULT`).

This was surfaced by the declarative-HCL cross-cluster validation (`posthog/clickhouse/hcl/check.sh`, chschema proxy column check). It is currently **masked** by a `known_drift_skip()` entry in `check.sh` (env `local`) — this issue is to fix the drift and drop that skip.

Evidence (live schema, per env)

From the introspected `PostHog/clickhouse-schema` dumps:

| table | dev | prod-us | prod-eu | local |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sharded_events_recent` (storage) | non-null | non-null | non-null | non-null |
| `events_recent` (Distributed) | non-null | non-null | non-null | **Nullable** |
| `distributed_events_recent` (Distributed) | **Nullable** | **Nullable** | **Nullable** | **Nullable** |

So:
- `distributed_events_recent.inserted_at` is `Nullable` on **every** node in every env — a genuine fleet-wide mismatch with storage.
- `events_recent.inserted_at` was already migrated to non-null in the **cloud** envs (see #47879, which added the non-nullable variant), but the base SQL definition and the **local** table were never updated — so local (and any fresh cluster) still creates it `Nullable`.

Root cause

`posthog/models/event/sql.py` has two constants:

- L37 `INSERTED_AT_COLUMN = ", inserted_at Nullable(DateTime64(6, 'UTC')) DEFAULT NOW64()"`
- L38 `INSERTED_AT_NOT_NULLABLE_COLUMN = ", inserted_at DateTime64(6, 'UTC') DEFAULT NOW64()"`

The Distributed proxies use the **Nullable** one, the storage uses the non-null one:

- L345 `EVENTS_RECENT_TABLE_SQL` → `... + INSERTED_AT_COLUMN`  (should be non-null)
- L361 `DISTRIBUTED_EVENTS_RECENT_TABLE_SQL` → `... + INSERTED_AT_COLUMN`  (should be non-null)
- L399 `SHARDED_EVENTS_RECENT_TABLE_SQL` → `... + INSERTED_AT_NOT_NULLABLE_COLUMN`  ✅ (storage, correct — leave as is)

Fix

Invoke the `/clickhouse-migrations` skill first. A `Distributed` table is metadata-only, so this is a **safe DROP + CREATE** (no data moved) — recreate the two proxies with non-null `inserted_at`.

1. In `posthog/models/event/sql.py`, switch `EVENTS_RECENT_TABLE_SQL` (L345) and `DISTRIBUTED_EVENTS_RECENT_TABLE_SQL` (L361) from `INSERTED_AT_COLUMN` to `INSERTED_AT_NOT_NULLABLE_COLUMN`. (`sharded_events_recent` already uses the non-null constant — do not change it.)
2. Add a migration in `posthog/clickhouse/migrations/` that recreates `events_recent` and `distributed_events_recent` with the corrected (non-null) column — `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ... ` + recreate from the updated SQL, on the appropriate `node_roles`. Recreate is idempotent where the column is already non-null (cloud `events_recent`), and corrects it everywhere else. Keep the PR migration-only.
3. Regenerate the HCL golden so the declarative source matches: `bash posthog/clickhouse/hcl/gen-golden.sh` + `bash posthog/clickhouse/hcl/gen-sql.sh`, then remove the `events_recent,distributed_events_recent` entry from `known_drift_skip()` in `posthog/clickhouse/hcl/check.sh`.

Acceptance criteria

- `events_recent` and `distributed_events_recent` declare `inserted_at DateTime64(6, 'UTC') DEFAULT now64()` (non-null), matching `sharded_events_recent`, on all node roles.
- The `local` entry of `known_drift_skip()` in `check.sh` is removed and `bash posthog/clickhouse/hcl/check.sh` is green (validate finds no `inserted_at` type mismatch).
- The multinode live-convergence gate (`ci-clickhouse-multinode-migrations.yml`) is green (the recreated tables match the regenerated golden).
- No change to `sharded_events_recent`.

- This continues the alignment started in #47879.
- Editing the HCL alone is not a fix — the HCL mirrors the live nodes (which are `Nullable`), so the golden matches and the gate is green today; the migration must change the cluster first, then the golden follows via `gen-golden.sh`.
